case_name: American Blind Community v. Tenet Healthcare Corporation
court: Federal court (specific district not confirmed in public sources)
defendant_revenue_band: >$10B (third-largest for-profit hospital chain in the US)
claim_type: ADA Title III and Rehabilitation Act Section 504 — hospital websites inaccessible via screen readers to visually impaired users
estimated_costs: Confidential settlement; parties settled shortly after filing

sources.name: Mintz Levin — The Rising Tide of ADA Litigation Against Health Care Entities

violation_source_evidence: Fredrikson & Byron legal alert (fredlaw.com/alert-healthcare-sector-is-newest-target-for-website-accessibility-lawsuits, January 2017): Tenet Healthcare hospital websites were 'not accessible to blind individuals using screen-reader technology.' No additional WCAG criteria specified in this Tier 2 source. Healthcare Weekly (healthcareweekly.com/ada-compliance-healthcare-websites) is Tier 3 and adds no specifics. No Tier 1 complaint or court document retrieved. Violations limited to what is documented in available sources.
summary_one_line: A class action on behalf of all Americans with visual disabilities sued Tenet Healthcare in 2016 for screen-reader-inaccessible hospital websites; parties settled shortly after filing — terms undisclosed.
notes: Filed 2016 as class action on behalf of all Americans with visual impairments. Facilities named include Hahnemann University Hospital, Hialeah Hospital, Coral Gables Hospital. Legal basis: both ADA Title III and Rehabilitation Act Section 504. Settled shortly after filing — no public terms. Marked use_in_report: false due to lack of Tier 1 sources with specific docket/court information. Docket unverified. Include only as supporting context for healthcare sector vulnerability.
